ai.description: This frog reaches 20–25 mm. It is brownish with a dark, hourglass-shaped dorsal pattern and a pale mid-dorsal stripe. Key features include a pointed snout and reduced webbing on the toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Microhyla mukhlesuri* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark, V-shaped or W-shaped mark on its back, which is absent in other similar Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Microhyla mukhlesuri* inhabits moist, low-altitude areas, typically found in tropical deciduous forests, bamboo thickets, and near agricultural wetlands or paddy fields.
ai.behavior: *Microhyla mukhlesuri* is primarily nocturnal, emerging after rainfall to forage for small invertebrates in leaf litter and moist soil near temporary water bodies.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Microhyla mukhlesuri* breeds in temporary pools during the monsoon (June–August), laying clutches of approximately 200–300 eggs that hatch into free-swimming larvae.
ai.distributionRemarks: Microhyla mukhlesuri is found in Northeast India (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura) and Bangladesh, typically inhabiting low-elevation plains and foothills.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Microhyla mukhlesuri* is a high-pitched, insect-like trill consisting of rapidly repeated pulses, typically heard from flooded rice fields or marshes.
